title: Commencing transition from 0.4 to 1.0
categories: UK digital verification services trust framework

content.text: Commencement of the transition period between the 0.4 and 1.0 versions of the trust framework and supplementary codes starts today
One of the conformity assessment bodies that are approved to certify against the UK digital verification services trust framework and the supplementary codes is now accredited to certify against:
In June, we set transition timelines for certified services as well as those that wish to get certified in the near future. These transition timelines commenced on 2 September 2026.

We have separately posted about the publication of the 1.1 versions of the right to work and right to rent supplementary codes, which are to be used with the 1.0 trust framework, and services uplifting their right to work or rent supplementary code certification from the 0.4 version will uplift directly to the 1.1 version.
What does it mean for you?

The CAB’s accreditation to certify against the 1.0 publication of the trust framework, and the 1.0 and 1.1 publications of the relevant supplementary codes, means that the transition period has begun as specified in section 0 of each publication.
Each service already certified has a minimum of 15 months to transition.

If your service currently holds certification against the 0.4 version of the trust framework, and/or the 0.4 versions of any of the supplementary codes, you should start thinking about when you would like to uplift its certification to the 1.0 version (or 1.1 version, in the case of the relevant supplementary codes). The options you have are outlined below.
Certification against the 1.0 version of the trust framework will also entitle you to use the CertifID trust mark.

If you have a new service that has not yet been certified against the trust framework, or an existing service that no longer holds a valid certification, you will follow the standard certification route.
Uplifting an existing certified service to 1.0
An approved and accredited CAB can certify your service against the 1.0 trust framework, and the 1.0 and 1.1 publications of the relevant supplementary codes, from 2nd September 2026.
All existing services will have a bespoke timeline for transition, based on their existing certification cycle. Every service will have at least 15 months to uplift.
If your service is already certified when the 1.0 trust framework comes into force, then:
By an “evaluation activity”, we mean either a surveillance audit or a full audit for services currently certified against the trust framework.
The same applies if your service is certified against the 0.4 version of one of the supplementary codes when the 1.0 or 1.1 versions come into force.
If you are certified against the 0.4 version of the DBS supplementary code, you will transition to the 1.0 version in the same fashion as for transition between the 0.4 and 1.0 trust framework.

If you are certified against the 0.4 version of the right to work and/or right to rent supplementary code, you will transition to the 1.1 version in the same fashion as for transition between the 0.4 and 1.0 trust framework.
You can choose to uplift sooner via a delta assessment
If you wish to uplift your service to the 1.0 trust framework sooner than your next evaluation activity you may be able to do so via an out-of-cycle delta assessment.
A delta assessment will only evaluate the rules that have changed between 0.4 and 1.0; it is not a full, top-to-bottom audit of your service.
Delta assessments are only available if your service:
You won't be able to have a delta assessment if your service is on a two-year cycle.

This delta assessment does not replace your ordinary cycle of evaluation activities. It will focus solely on the new requirements of the 1.0 trust framework. It enables you to make a choice of uplifting sooner than the service’s existing certification cycle, if you wish to.
New services
As of 2 September 2026, the 1.0 versions of the trust framework and DBS supplementary code, and the 1.1 versions of the right to work and right to rent supplementary codes are in force.
If your service is not currently certified and you want it to be, you will be evaluated against the in-force versions.
Start preparing for uplift
If you are a service provider, it is your responsibility to plan for and manage your uplift.
You should start to implement the 1.0 trust framework in your service from today, so you are ready to uplift. You should do the same for the 1.0 and 1.1 supplementary codes, as applicable.
You should also speak with your CAB to agree a plan for evaluating your service(s).
We believe this transition process gives every service provider a flexible, responsive uplift process that can meet its needs. If you have any questions you can contact either OfDIA or your CAB.
Services certified against 1.0 get a trust mark

We are very excited for this new trust framework, not only because it reflects the input from the industry and other key stakeholders, but also because certification against the 1.0 trust framework means issuance of the trust mark to services certified and registered against this version.
This is an exciting step for the ecosystem as the trust mark is another way of increasing trust in services that meet the requirements set by OfDIA.
